result.headline: Throttle command dropped to 0 at 73.3 s and stayed there; motor channel ch2 followed, aircraft lost altitude.
result.explanation: The propulsion loop (throttle and its output ch2) went to zero at t=73.3 s without a recorded mode change or event. ch2 follows the throttle command, so the cut came upstream of the output. Who commanded it is not in the data.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT propulsion.throttle was varying, then held 0 from t=73.346 s to the end of the recording (15.304 s, 39 samples)
evidence.shows: Throttle command went to 0 at 73.346 s and never recovered, with no event logged.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT actuator.output[ch[2]] was varying, then held 1100 from t=73.854 s to the end of the recording (14.7 s, 44 samples)
evidence.shows: Output ch2 sat at the 1100 us minimum for the rest of the flight, after the throttle command, not before it.

evidence.quote: ROLE actuator.output[ch[2]] follows propulsion.throttle (correlation 0.987 over the recording): it serves that loop
evidence.shows: ch2 is the throttle/propulsion output. It tracks the command at lag 0.335 s with correlation 0.998, so the output stage obeyed its command.

evidence.quote: ANOMALY a7 t=77.168 s: vehicle.attitude[pitch] followed control.attitude_setpoint[pitch] worse for good (typical |error| 0.984 -> 7.593)
evidence.shows: Pitch tracking degraded after the throttle cut. This is an effect.

evidence.quote: ANOMALY a10 t=79.55 s: vehicle.altitude[relative] changed level for good (49.791 -> 37.898 m)
evidence.shows: Altitude fell after the throttle cut, consistent with lost thrust.

checked.check: compare at 73.346 s: what changed at the throttle drop
checked.result: Throttle median 41 -> 0 and frozen (z 13.7). ch2 1428 -> 1100. Yaw, pitch and roll tracking errors all rose after it (ratios 3.21, 3.03, 1.77).
checked.about: Propulsion command cut as the onset

checked.check: sequence 55-82 s: which signals left baseline first
checked.result: Roll setpoint left baseline first (at 64.359 s), then roll (65.35 s). Throttle left baseline at 73.346 s and ch2 at 73.494 s. Pitch tracking worsened later.
ch2 and throttle unchanged (1444 -> 1452 us, 43 -> 44 %), z 1.0. The SHIFT line is a median-window artifact of the later drop.
checked.about: Early ch2 shift as the onset

checked.result: Correlation 0.984, best lag 0.335 s with correlation 0.998. The output follows the command.
checked.about: Fault inside the ch2 output or motor driver

checked.result: Throttle rose 5 -> 34 % and ch2 1136 -> 1372 us. This looks like take-off or start-up behaviour, and tracking is normal.
checked.about: Early velocity shifts as a fault

checked.result: The only event is the battery low-voltage WARN at 0.883 s. There are no mode, failsafe or RC events, and no earlier cases.
checked.about: Battery or failsafe as the cause

outcomes.label: Mode change or failsafe at 73.3 s
outcomes.means: The throttle cut was commanded by the system. The cause is the trigger of that mode or failsafe.
outcomes.then: Trace the failsafe trigger condition and its inputs

outcomes.label: Battery voltage collapse near 73 s
outcomes.means: Power-side cutoff or sag drove the throttle to zero.
outcomes.then: Review battery health and cutoff configuration

outcomes.label: No mode, RC or battery cause; ESC fault flags
outcomes.means: The controller sent zero or the motor driver stopped without any commanded event.
outcomes.then: Plan a bench test of the ESC and motor on ch2

unknowns: Who or what commanded throttle to 0 at 73.346 s; the recording shows no mode change or operator event.

data_requests.why_needed: Separates a commanded throttle cut from a controller, ESC or power fault.

unobservable.fact: Whether the motor and ESC on ch2 were physically healthy when thrust was lost
unobservable.why_it_matters: The recording holds the commanded PWM, not motor speed, so it cannot show a motor or ESC fault.
unobservable.how_to_observe: Bench-test the ESC and motor on ch2 and read ESC fault logs.

hypotheses.claim: The autopilot or operator commanded throttle to zero (mode change, failsafe or manual cut), not a hardware fault.
hypotheses.because: Throttle command drops first, with ch2 following shortly after. The recording shows no event, so the source is unknown.
hypotheses.observed_at: Recorded throttle command and PWM output

hypotheses.claim: The motor or ESC on ch2 failed or stopped, and the controller reduced the throttle in response.
hypotheses.because: ch2 follows the throttle command (lag 0.335 s, correlation 0.998), so the output stage obeyed. The recorded PWM cannot show motor state.

hypotheses.claim: Low battery voltage or a power cutoff forced throttle to zero.
hypotheses.because: A battery low-voltage WARN appears at 0.883 s, but it is a start-up line. No voltage signal is recorded to check at 73 s.

hypotheses.claim: Large roll excursions before the cut stressed the aircraft and led to the throttle drop.
hypotheses.because: Roll left baseline before the cut and the roll setpoint moved with it. Roll tracking stayed normal at 59.249 s, and no link to the cut is shown.

hypotheses.claim: A control-surface actuator (ch1, ch3-5) caused the fault.
hypotheses.because: Those channels keep responding and shift only after the throttle cut, so they look like effects.

events.what: Throttle command to 0 and ch2 held at 1100 us from about 73.3 s
events.why: Earliest persistent change in the propulsion loop; no mode event explains it.

events.what: Battery low voltage warning at 0.883 s
events.why: Start-up line. It matters only if later data links it to the cut.

events.what: Pitch, roll and yaw tracking worse, altitude falling, pitch setpoint shifted
events.why: Consequences of lost thrust, seconds after the cut.

events.what: ch2 and throttle SHIFT lines at 59.249 s and 69.68 s
events.why: Median-window artifacts of the later drop; compare at 59.249 shows no change.

events.what: velocity x and y level shifts at 20.189 s and 7.51 s
events.why: Take-off and early manoeuvre; throttle rose from start-up levels at 7.51 s and tracking was normal.

result.lesson: No earlier cases were available, so none apply.
result.reuse_when: Applies to a fixed-wing UAV running MAVROS/PX4-style control when the throttle command latches to 0 mid-flight with no mode or failsafe event while the other control channels keep responding.
